items.title: Russia, Ukraine and European security
items.actors:
- **Russia**: [[p:Vladimir Putin]]; Kremlin spokesman [[p:Dmitry Peskov]]; chief of the general staff [[p:Valery Gerasimov]].
- **Ukraine**: President [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and the Ukrainian armed forces.
- **United States**: President [[p:Donald Trump]] and envoy [[p:Steve Witkoff]], who broker the talks.
- **European states and [[p:NATO]]**: they arm and finance Ukraine and want a seat in the talks.
- **Belarus**: [[p:Alexander Lukashenko]], Moscow's closest ally and a staging ground in 2022.
- **Moldova** (with breakaway Transnistria) and the **Baltic states**: the front-line states.
items.timeline:
- **1991**: The Soviet Union dissolves and Ukraine becomes independent.
- **2014**: The [[e:Revolution of Dignity]] topples Yanukovych. Russia annexes Crimea, and a Russian-backed war starts in Donbas.
- **2015**: The [[e:Minsk agreements]] freeze but do not end the Donbas war.
- **Feb 2022**: Russia launches the [[e:Russian invasion of Ukraine|full-scale invasion]]. Kyiv holds, and Russia retreats from the north.
- **2022–2023**: Ukrainian counter-offensives retake Kharkiv oblast and Kherson city. The 2023 offensive stalls.
- **2024–2026**: A war of attrition in Donetsk oblast, with mass drone and missile strikes on both sides. Finland and Sweden join NATO.
- **2025–2026**: US-brokered [[e:Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|peace talks]] start and stall. Talks revive in October 2026.
items.disputes:
- **Territory**: Russia demands all of Donbas and recognition of its annexations. Kyiv refuses to cede land it holds.
- **Security guarantees**: whether Ukraine gets Western guarantees, foreign troops or a NATO path.
- **Sanctions**: their scope, and how US and EU policy diverge.
- **Frozen Russian assets** and Ukraine's long-term funding.
- **Europe's role**: whether Europeans sit at the table or a US–Russia deal is made over their heads.
items.current:
Diplomacy is racing a US clock. Washington reportedly wants a settlement before Democrats take Congress in January, and after the [[p:Coalition of the willing (Russo-Ukrainian war)|coalition of the willing]] met in Berlin on 19 Nov, the US proposed a four-way Ukraine–Europe–US–Russia round before Christmas. [[p:Yuri Ushakov]] has invited the French, German and British security advisers to Moscow, while [[p:Vladimir Putin]] refuses local ceasefires after Ukraine's repeated strikes on the [[p:Crimean Bridge]] and [[p:Sergey Lavrov]] calls Kyiv 'Russian land'.

The front moves slowly, with Russian infiltration into Kostiantynivka and see-saw fighting near Dobropillia. The air and sea war is widening. Russia's 20 Nov barrage was among the largest of the war and a strike on Dymer killed 11. Ukraine keeps hitting refineries as far as Perm, forcing Moscow to allow lower-grade gasoline, and on 22 Nov it sank a Russian corvette at Benghazi, its first claimed strike in the Mediterranean.

On NATO's flank, Kh-101 missiles landed at three sites in Poland on 20 Nov; Warsaw took the case to the [[p:North Atlantic Council]] without invoking Article 4. A drone-hit Russian military cargo ship burned in Finnish waters, Kaliningrad had its first air alert of the war, and drones keep hitting merchant ships off Bulgaria and Romania. Estonia closes its Russian crossings on 1 Dec, the EU readies a 22nd sanctions package and the US decides on troop levels in Europe in early December. Gagauzia votes in a governor runoff on 29 Nov.

items.title: The Middle East
items.actors:
- **Israel**: PM [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] and the IDF.
- **Palestinians**: [[p:Hamas]] in Gaza, and the [[p:Palestinian Authority]] in the West Bank.
- **Iran**: the government and the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]], with allied groups such as [[p:Hezbollah]] in Lebanon and the [[p:Houthis]] in Yemen.
- **United States**: at war with Iran since February 2026.
- **Gulf states**: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar. Turkey, Egypt, Jordan and Pakistan act as mediators.
items.timeline:
- **1948**: Israel is founded. The 1967 war brings the West Bank and Gaza under Israeli control.
- **1979**: The Iranian revolution makes Iran the region's main anti-US and anti-Israel power.
- **2011**: The Arab uprisings, followed by civil wars in Syria, Yemen and Libya.
- **2015**: The [[e:Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|Iran nuclear deal]]. The US leaves it in 2018.
- **2020**: Under the [[e:Abraham Accords]], Israel normalises ties with the UAE, Bahrain and others.
- **7 Oct 2023**: The Hamas attack on Israel starts the [[e:Gaza war]]. It spreads to Lebanon, the Red Sea and direct Israel–Iran exchanges.
- **Jun 2025**: The [[e:Twelve-Day War]]. Israel and the US strike Iran's nuclear sites.
- **Feb 2026**: US–Israeli strikes start the [[e:2026 Iran war]]. A June interim deal collapses in July, and Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz to "non-compliant" shipping.
items.disputes:
- **Iran**: its nuclear programme and enriched uranium stockpile, and IAEA access.
- **Shipping**: control of the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea lanes.
- **Palestinians**: statehood, and the future of Gaza and the West Bank, including settlements.
- **Lebanon**: Hezbollah's arms and Israel's presence in the south.
- **Saudi–Houthi war**: the Saudi–Houthi conflict in Yemen and its spread to Saudi cities.
items.current:
The [[e:2026 Iran war]] remains in an armed pause that is fraying fast. The US keeps its [[e:2026 United States naval blockade of Iran|naval blockade]] and [[p:Donald Trump]] threatens to sink any ship that runs it; Iran calls the blockade aggression, vows 'all available means' against it and keeps Hormuz shut to most traffic, saying it reopens only if sanctions and the blockade go and the [[e:Islamabad Talks|Islamabad]] memorandum is honoured. Seven tankers have been hit since 16 Nov, the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] keeps striking US sites in Bahrain and Kuwait, and Qatar carries messages between the two sides.

The Saudi–[[p:Houthis|Houthi]] war has turned against the Yemeni government: after taking ground in Lahj the Houthis are about 60 km from Aden and massing on the Al-Bayda–Abyan front, while firing at Saudi refineries and Riyadh. In Iraq, a joint state force is replacing [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]] at Jurf al-Sakhar after a deal reportedly brokered by Iran.

In Israel, [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] holds the mandate and a Knesset majority and is negotiating with [[p:Likud]] while threatening a minority government. Israel's first large ground push in central Gaza since the 2025 ceasefire has brought daily deadly strikes, settler arson in the West Bank continues, and the UN has still named no successor to [[p:United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]] before it ends on 31 December. In Turkey, courts keep removing [[p:Ekrem İmamoğlu]] from the 2028 race.

items.title: East and Southeast Asia
items.actors:
- **China**: [[p:Xi Jinping]] and the [[p:Chinese Communist Party]], the PLA and the China Coast Guard.
- **Taiwan**: President [[p:Lai Ching-te]].
- **North Korea**: [[p:Kim Jong Un]].
- **South Korea**, and **Japan** under PM [[p:Sanae Takaichi]].
- **United States**: its alliances with Japan, South Korea and the Philippines.
- **[[p:ASEAN]]**: Myanmar's military-led state, and the [[p:Arakan Army]] and other resistance forces.
items.timeline:
- **1949**: The Communist victory in China's civil war. The Nationalists retreat to Taiwan.
- **1950–1953**: The [[e:Korean War]] ends in an armistice, not a peace treaty.
- **1978**: Deng's reforms begin China's rise. Its WTO entry follows in 2001.
- **2006**: North Korea's first nuclear test. Its arsenal grows despite sanctions.
- **2016**: An arbitral tribunal rejects China's sweeping South China Sea claims. Beijing ignores the ruling.
- **2021**: The [[e:2021 Myanmar coup d'état|Myanmar coup]] starts a nationwide civil war.
- **2022–2025**: Large PLA drills around Taiwan, Philippine–Chinese clashes at Second Thomas Shoal, and the US–China tariff war.
- **2026**: APEC is hosted by China (Shenzhen, November), with a possible Trump–Xi–Putin meeting.
items.disputes:
- **Taiwan**: its status, and PLA pressure on the island.
- **South China Sea**: sovereignty over its reefs, especially Second Thomas Shoal and Scarborough Shoal.
- **Korea**: North Korea's nuclear and missile programmes, and the inter-Korean border (the 2026 DMZ landmine row).
- **US–China**: tariffs and technology controls.
- **Myanmar**: its civil war, and the junta's return to ASEAN.
items.current:
After [[e:APEC China 2026]] in Shenzhen, the US–China truce holds: Beijing has extended its suspension of gallium, germanium and antimony export bans on the US to 27 Jan, while rare-earth curbs and the 24% tariff stay suspended to 10 Jan. But Washington is preparing new Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others, and Taiwan's stock market fell almost 5%. At home, Xi's anti-corruption drive has reached Shanghai party chief [[p:Chen Jining]], the fourth Politburo member to fall this term.

Taiwan votes on 28 Nov in local elections and a nuclear referendum, amid indictments for Chinese-funded interference and a $14bn US arms sale still frozen. Japan's [[p:Sanae Takaichi]] got only a handshake from Xi. Chinese vessels near the Philippines more than doubled after the ASEAN summit.

In Korea, the Supreme Court ruled the [[e:2024 South Korean martial law]] an insurrection, and [[p:Lee Jae Myung]] replaced his foreign minister and spy chief. The IAEA says North Korea has expanded enrichment at Yongbyon while [[p:Kim Jong Un]] ignores Trump. Mongolia's parliament accepted President [[p:Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh]]'s resignation, so a snap election is due within four months.

In Southeast Asia, Indonesian police named ex-police chief [[p:Listyo Sigit Prabowo]] a treason suspect as the Prabowo–Jokowi rift deepens, and the MPR picks a new vice president on 11 Dec. The [[p:International Court of Justice]] found Myanmar responsible for the [[e:Rohingya genocide]], and the junta says it is rethinking ties with ASEAN. [[p:Rodrigo Duterte]]'s ICC trial opens on 30 Nov.

items.title: The Americas
items.actors:
- **United States**: President [[p:Donald Trump]] and Secretary of State [[p:Marco Rubio]].
- **Brazil**: [[p:Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] and [[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]].
- **Venezuela**: the interim government of [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]], and the opposition led by [[p:María Corina Machado]].
- **Cuba**: [[p:Miguel Díaz-Canel]].
- **Mexico**: [[p:Claudia Sheinbaum]]. Canada, Colombia, Argentina ([[p:Javier Milei]]) and Peru.
items.timeline:
- **1823**: The Monroe Doctrine.
- **1959**: The Cuban revolution is followed by a US embargo from 1962.
- **1994**: NAFTA, replaced by the USMCA in 2020.
- **1999–2013**: Chávez's "Bolivarian" Venezuela. The Maduro era brings collapse and mass emigration.
- **2025**: Trump's second term brings sweeping tariffs and military strikes on alleged drug boats.
- **Jan 2026**: US forces capture [[p:Nicolás Maduro]]. An energy blockade of Cuba follows.
- **2026**: A rightward electoral swing (Colombia, Peru). Brazil's runoff is on 25 October and the US midterms on 3 November.
items.disputes:
- **Trade**: US tariffs on Canada and Mexico, and the USMCA review.
- **Venezuela**: its transition and an election date.
- **Cuba**: US pressure, and calls for regime change.
- **Migration and drug cartels**: US unilateral force against them.
- **Brazil**: its political polarisation and relations with the US.
items.current:
Democrats will hold the House and 56 of 100 Senate seats from January after flipping Alaska and Mississippi in the [[e:midterms|2026 United States elections]], and House Democrats have nominated [[p:Hakeem Jeffries]] for Speaker. [[p:Donald Trump]] faces a Congress keen to curb the [[e:2026 Iran war|Iran war]] and the tariffs, and an 11 Dec funding deadline in the lame duck. Abroad, Trump held the first US–China–Russia leaders' meeting with [[p:Xi Jinping]] and [[p:Vladimir Putin]] in Shenzhen on 19 Nov; no nuclear deal emerged.

Trade with neighbours is stuck: the [[e:USMCA|United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement]] is under rolling review after Washington declined to renew it, Canada faces 50% tariffs on some goods and is cutting its own deals with Beijing, and Mexico still faces Section 232 duties. In Venezuela, [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]]'s interim government is following a US roadmap that starts with a new supreme court by mid-December, while public-sector unions strike over wages. Washington is tightening Cuba sanctions and Trump has floated force.

Lula starts a fourth term in January and is pushing a fiscal adjustment bill; [[p:Javier Milei]] will seek re-election in 2027; Paraguay's ousted president [[p:Santiago Peña]] is in detention; Salvadoran troops fight gangs in Haiti. ([Israel National News](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/436608), [Just Security](https://www.justsecurity.org/165038/early-edition-november-18-2026/), [CP24](https://www.cp24.com/news/world/2026/11/17/carney-and-sheinbaum-meet-at-summit-in-china-as-both-navigate-trumps-tumult/), [El Diario](https://eldiario.com/2026/11/16/resumen-noticias-venezuela-16-noviembre/))

items.title: Africa
items.actors:
- **Sudan**: the army under [[p:Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] against the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF).
- **Ethiopia**: PM [[p:Abiy Ahmed]], the [[p:Tigray People's Liberation Front]] and Eritrea.
- **DRC**: the government and the M23-derived rebellion, now led by [[p:Joseph Kabila]]. Rwanda.
- **Sahel juntas** (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger), the jihadist group [[p:Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal-Muslimin]] and Russia's Africa Corps.
- **The [[p:African Union]]** and Gulf powers (the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar).
items.timeline:
- **1960s**: Decolonisation. The OAU (later the AU) freezes colonial borders.
- **1994**: The Rwandan genocide, followed by the Congo wars of 1996–2003.
- **2011**: South Sudan's independence and the fall of Gaddafi.
- **2012 onwards**: Insurgency in the Sahel. Coups in Mali (2020–21), Burkina Faso (2022) and Niger (2023) bring juntas that turn to Russia.
- **2020–2022**: The [[e:Tigray war]] ends with the Pretoria deal.
- **Apr 2023**: The [[e:Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]] begins. The RSF takes El Fasher in October 2025.
- **2026**: The Ethiopia–Tigray war resumes (September), a large Ebola (Bundibugyo) epidemic hits DRC, and Mali's army retakes Kidal.
items.disputes:
- **Sudan**: power, and Gulf backing for the warring sides.
- **Ethiopia**: Tigray's status, and Ethiopia's quest for sea access versus Eritrea.
- **Eastern DRC**: minerals and Rwanda's role there.
- **The Sahel**: jihadist expansion and the shift from France to Russia.
- **Western Sahara**: its status. The UN's MINURSO mission lapsed in October 2026 after a Russian veto.
items.current:
Overlapping wars, an Ebola epidemic and an unmonitored Western Sahara define the continent.

- **Sudan**: The [[p:Sudanese Armed Forces]] have the momentum in Kordofan, taking ground in West Kordofan for the first time since May 2025 and closing on En Nahud as [[p:Rapid Support Forces]] commanders defect. The RSF is pushing south of Ad Damazin in Blue Nile. A UN report says drones caused about three-quarters of verified civilian deaths this year.
- **Ethiopia–Eritrea**: After federal forces took Mekelle in October, the Tigray war has turned into a direct border confrontation, with reported drone and artillery exchanges around Badme and the army chief blaming Asmara and Cairo. Eritrea denies involvement.
- **Eastern DRC**: The rebellion led by [[p:Joseph Kabila]] (the FRN, which absorbed AFC/M23) is advancing west of Kahuzi-Biega towards Walikale and fighting in the Uvira–Fizi highlands; over 320,000 were newly displaced in early November. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has passed 11,300 cases and is still not under control.
- **Somalia**: The government rejects a Supreme Court ruling against President [[p:Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]]'s term extension and installed a new chief justice; the main opposition no longer recognises him, and he has broken openly with the UAE.
- **North Africa**: Egypt confirmed troops are deployed in Saudi Arabia against [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] attacks. In Western Sahara, the [[p:Polisario Front]] declared a general mobilisation after the UN mission's mandate lapsed; Morocco says it respects the ceasefire.
- **Sahel and South Africa**: JNIM's fuel blockade of Bamako continues, and Burkina's junta issued warrants against exiled journalists. In South Africa, coalition talks after the ANC's worst-ever local result decide the Gauteng metros by late November.

([Reuters/Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261118/ethiopia-and-eritrea-amass-forces-along-border-heightening-war-fears-sources-say), [Actualite.cd](https://actualite.cd/2026/11/12/rdc-la-suite-dintenses-combats-au-sud-kivu-plus-de-323-000-deplaces-enregistres-en), [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/11/18/al-burhans-forces-push-towards-rsf-stronghold-as-un-warns-of-sudan-drone-toll/), [TSA](https://www.tsa-algerie.com/sahara-occidental-le-polisario-decrete-la-mobilisation-generale/))

items.title: South and Central Asia
items.actors:
- **India**: PM [[p:Narendra Modi]].
- **Pakistan**: the army under [[p:Asim Munir]] and the civilian government. Imran Khan's [[p:Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf]] (PTI).
- **Afghanistan**: the [[p:Taliban]] government. The [[p:Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]] (TTP).
- **Bangladesh** and **Nepal**: new post-uprising governments.
- **Central Asia**: the five states, with Russia, China and the US competing for influence.
- **The Caucasus**: Armenia (Pashinyan), Azerbaijan (Aliyev), and Georgia, ruled by [[p:Georgian Dream]].
items.timeline:
- **1947**: Partition creates India and Pakistan. Their wars over Kashmir follow in 1947, 1965 and 1999.
- **1991**: The Soviet collapse gives the Central Asian and Caucasus states independence.
- **2001–2021**: The US-led war in Afghanistan ends with the Taliban's return.
- **2020–2023**: Azerbaijan retakes Nagorno-Karabakh.
- **May 2025**: The [[e:2025 India–Pakistan conflict|India–Pakistan conflict]] after the Pahalgam attack.
- **2024–2025**: Uprisings topple governments in Bangladesh (2024) and Nepal (2025).
- **2026**: A Pakistan–Taliban war, Bangladesh's elected government under Tarique Rahman, and an Armenia–Azerbaijan peace process.
items.disputes:
- **India and Pakistan**: Kashmir and the Indus waters.
- **Pakistan and Afghanistan**: the Durand Line and the TTP's sanctuaries.
- **Armenia and Azerbaijan**: the peace treaty and transit routes.
- **Georgia**: its democratic backsliding.
- **Central Asia**: competition between Russia, China and the US over energy and minerals.
items.current:
The war between Pakistan and the Afghan [[p:Taliban]], which began with Pakistani airstrikes in February 2026, has settled into border skirmishes and near-daily fighting with the [[p:Pakistani Taliban|Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]] in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has been under federal emergency rule since October; Baloch separatists now use armed drones. Islamabad refuses to recognise the Taliban, excluded Afghanistan from the November ECO meeting, and keeps deporting Afghans, while acting as a go-between in the US–Iran war. Jailed ex-PM [[p:Imran Khan]]'s appeals are before the Islamabad High Court.

India–Pakistan hostility persists over Kashmir and the suspended [[p:Indus Waters Treaty]]; India's interim trade deal with the US awaits a new US tariff framework. Bangladesh faces arson during lockdowns by the banned [[p:Awami League]] as [[p:Sheikh Hasina]] vows to return from India, and the Ganges water treaty expires on 12 Dec. Nepal's PM [[p:Balen Shah]] faces a united opposition at home and visits India on 22–23 Nov. Sri Lanka is passing its last budget under the IMF programme amid rate rises.

In the Caucasus, [[p:Nikol Pashinyan]] is staking his job on a constitutional referendum that Azerbaijan demands before signing the peace treaty, while the US-backed TRIPP route is in technical talks; Georgia's Constitutional Court is weighing a ban on five opposition parties. In Central Asia, Kazakhstan's corruption purge has reached the heads of its wealth fund and railway, Kyrgyzstan votes for president on 27 Jan 2027, and Russia and the US are both courting Tajikistan. ([Arab News](https://www.arabnews.pk/pakistan/pakistan-says-it-excluded-afghanistan-from-regional-conference-over-taliban-recognition-3007593), [AFP via Manila Times](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/21/world/asia-oceania/fresh-arson-attacks-erupt-in-bangladesh-amid-unrest/2474967), [APA](https://en.apa.az/cis-countries/pashinyan-vows-not-to-run-for-prime-minister-in-next-elections-if-new-constitution-is-adopted-537142))

items.title: EU politics and cross-cutting issues
items.actors:
- **EU leaders**: Commission President [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]], European Council President [[p:António Costa]] and foreign-policy chief [[p:Kaja Kallas]].
- **The [[p:European Parliament]]** and the [[p:European Central Bank]] under [[p:Christine Lagarde]].
- **Member state leaders**: Germany ([[p:Friedrich Merz]]), France (Macron, with PM [[p:Sébastien Lecornu]]), Poland ([[p:Donald Tusk]]), Italy ([[p:Giorgia Meloni]]) and Hungary ([[p:Péter Magyar]]).
- **Global bodies**: the [[p:United Nations Security Council]], the [[p:International Atomic Energy Agency]] and [[p:OPEC]].
items.timeline:
- **1957**: The Treaty of Rome. The 1992 Maastricht Treaty creates the EU and the path to the euro.
- **2004–2013**: Eastern enlargement, from 15 members to 28.
- **2010–2012**: The eurozone debt crisis.
- **2015**: The migration crisis.
- **2016–2020**: [[e:Brexit]].
- **2022**: Russia's invasion leads to the EU's sanctions packages, a break with Russian gas, and candidate status for Ukraine and Moldova.
- **2026**: Hungary's change of government (Magyar), Ukraine's accession clusters opening, an energy shock from the Iran war, and talks on the 2028–34 budget.
items.disputes:
- **Enlargement**: its pace (Ukraine, Moldova, the Western Balkans), and vetoes.
- **The budget**: the 2028–34 long-term budget, and financing Ukraine.
- **Energy**: security and the Russian LNG phase-out.
- **Rule of law and populism** in member states.
- **Relations with the US**: transatlantic trade and security ties.
- **Arms control**: nuclear arms control after New START.
- **UN**: the paralysis of the Security Council and the 2026 Secretary-General selection.
items.current:
Europe heads into a budget-and-Ukraine summit week with one veto gone and another looming.

- **Money**: [[p:António Costa]] has tabled a [[p:2028–34 budget|Multiannual Financial Framework]] box about 10% below the Commission's plan. The Commission wants up to €45bn more for Ukraine in 2027, borrowed by the EU and repaid only from Russian reparations, which needs unanimity. [[p:Robert Fico]] says Slovakia will not join. Leaders meet on 26–27 Nov; the fallback is the 17–18 Dec summit.
- **Enlargement**: Hungary lifted its block on screening reports for Ukraine's and Moldova's clusters 4 and 5 on 20 Nov; openings could come in December. Montenegro has closed 25 of 33 chapters and aims to finish this year. Serbia's new parliament sits and a presidential vote is due in December.
- **Russia**: a 22nd sanctions package is ready to be tabled; the E5-plus-EU team is Europe's channel into the Ukraine talks.
- **Energy**: gas storage was about 69% on 20 Nov, far below normal for the season.
- **Domestic strain**: France's budgets face a 26 Nov deadline; Belgium's government has until 23 Nov to agree a budget; Sweden still has no government; Spain votes on 29 Nov with the right ahead in polls; Poland's [[p:Constitutional Tribunal|Constitutional Tribunal (Poland)]] leadership has been suspended by rival judges.

Globally, the Shenzhen meeting produced only a declaratory nuclear statement, the UN Secretary-General race is deadlocked after nine straw polls, and [[e:COP31|2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] ran into overtime without fossil-fuel language. ([European Pravda](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/20/7250427/); [EUalive](https://eualive.net/costa-trims-eu-budget-proposal-by-10-to-woo-frugal-states-ahead-of-summit/))
